Violago]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Partido Federal ng Pilipinas}}|border=darkgray}} [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas|PFP]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Majority }} '''Bulacan's 3rd congressional district''' is one of the seven [[congressional districts of the Philippines|congressional districts]] in the province of [[Bulacan]], [[Philippines]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] since 1987.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 11, 2021 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district consists of municipalities in northern and eastern Bulacan, namely [[Doña Remedios Trinidad]], [[San Ildefonso, Bulacan|San Ildefonso]], [[San Miguel, Bulacan|San Miguel]], and [[San Rafael, Bulacan|San Rafael]].{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=February 11, 2021}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Cholo Violago]] of the [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas]] (PFP).{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/house-members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=July 27, 2025}} [[Angat, Bulacan|Angat]] and [[Norzagaray]] were once part of the district until they were excised to form the [[Bulacan's 6th congressional district|sixth district]] effective 2022.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=11546|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2021/05/26/republic-act-no-11546/|publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)|Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines]]|date=August 13, 2021|access-date=August 13, 2021|title=An Act Reapportioning the Province of Bulacan into Six (6) Legislative Districts}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 |Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
